answer: In an agent marketplace, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked for 30 days, not by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 votes, so a sybil swarm gains no extra influence. An attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens to dominate. Even if identities cost less than copper, the market is no oasis for sockpuppets: every thread of voting power carries the same capital cost.
